::: {.jc-lede}
In 1987 Robert Solow quipped that you could see the computer age everywhere but in the productivity statistics. Brynjolfsson, Rock & Syverson (2018) built the escape hatch: general-purpose technologies demand years of *complementary, intangible* investment before they show up in output. Measured productivity flatlines — or dips — during the build-out, then inflects. A **J-curve**. This page is the running scoreboard for one bet: **AI is in the trough.**
:::

::: {.jc-links}
Full argument → [The Trough Looks Like Failure](/posts/2026-07-02-the-trough-looks-like-failure/) · Sources → [Brynjolfsson](/people/erik-brynjolfsson.qmd), [the J-Curve paper](/sources/the-productivity-j-curve.qmd)
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

jc = pd.read_parquet(Path("../../analysis/outputs/jcurve_sample.parquet"))
jc["date"] = pd.to_datetime(jc["date"]).dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
ojs_define(jc_data=jc.to_dict(orient="records"))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import { Plot } from "npm:@observablehq/plot"

jc = jc_data.map(d => ({...d, date: new Date(d.date)}))
last = a => a[a.length - 1]
idx = key => jc.map(d => ({date: d.date, value: d[key] / jc[0][key] * 100}))
raw = key => jc.map(d => ({date: d.date, value: d[key]}))
fmtPct = v => `${v > 0 ? "+" : ""}${v.toFixed(0)}%`

twoLine = (a, b, w, h, extra = {}) => Plot.plot({
  width: w, height: h, marginLeft: 30, marginBottom: 20, marginTop: 12, marginRight: 10,
  x: {type: "utc", label: null, ticks: 4, tickFormat: "%y"},
  y: {label: null, grid: true, ...(extra.y || {})},
  style: {fontFamily: "DM Mono, monospace", fontSize: "9px"},
  marks: [
    ...(extra.baseline != null ? [Plot.ruleY([extra.baseline], {stroke: "#C8C3B8", strokeDasharray: "2,3"})] : []),
    Plot.lineY(a.data, {x: "date", y: "value", stroke: a.color, strokeWidth: 1.9}),
    Plot.lineY(b.data, {x: "date", y: "value", stroke: b.color, strokeWidth: 1.9, strokeDasharray: b.dash || null}),
    Plot.dot([last(a.data)], {x: "date", y: "value", r: 3, fill: a.color}),
    Plot.dot([last(b.data)], {x: "date", y: "value", r: 3, fill: b.color})
  ]
})

inputsChart = twoLine({data: idx("adoption"), color: "#7C6FB5"}, {data: idx("it_investment"), color: "#4A6FA5"}, 380, 200)
payoffChart = twoLine({data: raw("productivity"), color: "#3A7D5E"}, {data: raw("tfp"), color: "#9A8F7A"}, 380, 200, {baseline: 100, y: {domain: [92, 122]}})

recalcData = jc.map(d => ({date: d.date, meas: d.productivity, adj: d.productivity_adj}))
recalcChart = Plot.plot({
  width: 660, height: 250, marginLeft: 32, marginBottom: 24, marginTop: 16, marginRight: 60,
  x: {type: "utc", label: null, ticks: 5, tickFormat: "%Y"},
  y: {label: null, grid: true},
  style: {fontFamily: "DM Mono, monospace", fontSize: "10px"},
  marks: [
    Plot.areaY(recalcData, {x: "date", y1: "meas", y2: "adj", fill: "#3A7D5E", fillOpacity: 0.10}),
    Plot.lineY(recalcData, {x: "date", y: "meas", stroke: "#6A6A6A", strokeWidth: 1.8}),
    Plot.lineY(recalcData, {x: "date", y: "adj", stroke: "#3A7D5E", strokeWidth: 1.8, strokeDasharray: "3,3"}),
    Plot.text([last(recalcData)], {x: "date", y: "adj", text: ["adjusted"], dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 9, fill: "#3A7D5E"}),
    Plot.text([last(recalcData)], {x: "date", y: "meas", text: ["measured"], dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 9, fill: "#6A6A6A"})
  ]
})
```

<h2 class="sec-kicker">Inputs vs. payoff</h2>
<p class="sec-dek">The whole thesis, in two pictures: the inputs are surging; the payoff isn't in the measured numbers — yet.</p>

<h2 class="sec-kicker">The recalculation</h2>

::: {.jc-recalc-body}
The paradox may be partly an accounting artifact. When firms pour people and money into *building* AI capability — process redesign, data pipelines, retraining — that intangible investment is largely uncounted in output. So measured productivity **understates** what's actually being built during the trough. The dashed line adds back a rough intangibles wedge; the shaded gap is Brynjolfsson's argument in one shape: the payoff may already exist, just not where the official statistics are looking.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false

```
